title: Theo and the Thorn
premise: Ulyana Zhou, exiled from her storm-calling order for a crime she didn't commit, survives by guiding smugglers through the Thornfell mountains—until a scholar named Theo Bramble arrives carrying a century-old prophecy book that names her as the one who will 'reforge the covenant or bury both realms in winter.' The covenant between the human lowlands and the mountain's fae courts is failing, and its collapse unleashes an endless winter that devours border villages. Hunted by her former order, courted by two rival fae factions, and reluctantly bonded to Theo, whose blood ties him to the prophecy's original author, Ulyana must gather the three shattered keystones of the old pact. In the end she learns her exile was engineered to keep her from the truth—that she is half-fae, the living keystone—and she sacrifices her hard-won invisibility, binding herself to the mountain as its new storm-warden while choosing Theo and a found family of outcasts over the belonging she was denied.
about_author: Dominic Halloran is a former alpine search-and-rescue volunteer who writes fantasy shaped by real mountains, bad weather, and the people who live stubbornly inside both. He lives in a drafty farmhouse with his partner, two dogs, and an ever-growing collection of antique maps.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She guides a contraband caravan through a hidden pass during a freak early snowstorm, showing her mastery of Thornfell and her careful anonymity. Emotional beat: competence masking loneliness; she counts her money and counts her exits.

chapters.title: A Stranger with a Book
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The nervous scholar arrives at Ulyana's waystation inn, clutching a water-damaged prophecy book and asking for a guide no one else will hire. Emotional beat: wary curiosity; Ulyana refuses him twice before seeing her own name inked on a page a century old.

chapters.title: Ink Older Than Grief
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She reads the prophecy describing 'the exile who calls storms' and tonight's date exactly. Panic wars with denial as she burns the page—only for the words to reappear. Emotional beat: dread; her invisibility has been an illusion all along.

chapters.title: Terms of Passage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He negotiates passage, revealing only fragments: the book came from a burned archive, and someone killed to send it with him. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; two liars agreeing to need each other.

chapters.title: First Frost on the Border
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They reach the lowland village of Marrowgate and find frost in midsummer, crops blackened, and villagers whispering about the 'long winter' returning. Emotional beat: horror made domestic; this is what covenant failure looks like.

chapters.title: The Order Finds Her
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Storm-callers from her former order arrive hunting the prophecy book, led by her old mentor Serapha, who offers pardon if Ulyana surrenders it. Emotional beat: betrayal reopened; the past has teeth.

chapters.title: Running the Goat's Teeth
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A chase through a knife-edged ridge system; Ulyana uses forbidden storm-craft to save them, breaking her exile oath. Emotional beat: exhilaration and guilt; every use of power draws the order closer.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They shelter in a cavern-city of fae who lost their court when the covenant broke—hollow-eyed, fading, neither hostile nor whole. Emotional beat: pity; the war's victims were never human.

chapters.title: Briar and Bargain
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The hollow queen Vess offers the first keystone's location in exchange for a promise Ulyana can't yet name. Emotional beat: temptation; help always costs more than coin.

chapters.title: What Theo Won't Say
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Ulyana catches him burning letters from home; flashbacks reveal his grandmother wrote the prophecy book and died protecting it. Emotional beat: mirrored secrets; both are running from family legacies.

chapters.title: Keystone One: The Bell of Hours
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In a drowned chapel they retrieve the first keystone, waking a guardian that tests them with visions of their worst choices. Emotional beat: exposure; the guardian shows Ulyana the night of her alleged crime—and her memory doesn't match the official story.

chapters.title: The Lie That Exiled Me
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Shaken, she reconstructs her trial: evidence forged, witnesses coached, Serapha silent. Emotional beat: rage crystallizing into purpose; justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: Marrowgate Burns
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Returning to warn the village, they find the order has 'quarantined' it—burning it to stop the winter's spread, killing the infected. Emotional beat: grief and fury; institutional justice as atrocity.

chapters.title: The Outcasts' Camp
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Survivors of Marrowgate join them: gruff ferrywoman Dagny, feral child Pip, and a defected storm-caller, Ivo. Emotional beat: warmth kindling; a found family forms around shared abandonment.

chapters.title: Winter's Herald
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He explains the covenant's mechanics: three keystones, one warden, and a sacrifice clause everyone hopes is metaphorical. Emotional beat: foreboding; the fine print is written in blood.

chapters.title: The Gilded Court's Envoy
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A radiant envoy from the surviving fae court offers Ulyana sanctuary, legitimacy, everything—if she delivers the keystones to them instead. Emotional beat: seduction of belonging; the offer is almost enough.

chapters.title: Pip's Map
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. The child, who sees fae roads adults can't, leads them through a shortcut that shouldn't exist. Emotional beat: wonder; the smallest outcast becomes indispensable.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Sorrow Bridge
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Serapha's hunters attack; Dagny is gravely wounded holding the bridge. Ulyana unleashes a full storm for the first time in years. Emotional beat: cost of power; victory tastes like ash.

chapters.title: Tending Wounds, Trading Truths
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. While Dagny fights fever, Ulyana and Theo finally trade their full histories by firelight. Emotional beat: intimacy; trust built from mutual damage.

chapters.title: The Prophecy's Second Half
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Restoration magic reveals pages hidden in the book's binding: the warden must be 'of both bloods.' Ulyana goes very quiet. Emotional beat: dawning identity crisis.

chapters.title: Half-Blood
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Confronting Vess, Ulyana learns her mother was fae—a hollow-court noble—and her exile was arranged to keep her from ever learning it. Emotional beat: vertigo; her whole life was a containment strategy.

chapters.title: Serapha's Confession
chapters.summary: Serapha's POV. Captured after another skirmish, Serapha admits she helped forge the evidence—not from malice, but because the order feared what Ulyana was. Emotional beat: complicated mercy; Ulyana can't forgive, but understands.

chapters.title: Keystone Two: The Rootcrown
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Deep beneath Thornfell, they take the second keystone from a living tree-heart, awakening the mountain itself. Emotional beat: awe; the land is a sleeping witness.

chapters.title: The Mountain Speaks
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The mountain shows her the original covenant-making: her ancestor, also half-blood, binding realms with willing sacrifice. Emotional beat: inheritance; she is the latest hand on an old rope.

chapters.title: The Gilded Court Moves
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The gilded court, tired of waiting, seizes the camp and takes the keystones and hostages—including Pip. Emotional beat: desperation; diplomacy has failed.

chapters.title: Parley Under Banners
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana walks alone into the gilded court to negotiate, trading her surrender for the hostages' freedom. Emotional beat: courage; she finally stops running.

chapters.title: The Court's True Winter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo discovers the gilded court caused the covenant's decay deliberately, to force a new warden they could control. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the villain was the beautiful option all along.

chapters.title: Escape from Glass and Gold
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip frees the prisoners using fae roads, guided by the fading hollow queen Vess's last strength. Emotional beat: defiance; the small and broken strike back.

chapters.title: Vess's Last Light
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The hollow queen spends herself shattering the gilded court's gate, dying with her court's name restored. Emotional beat: elegy; redemption purchased at the final price.

chapters.title: Keystone Three: The Unmade Oath
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The third keystone isn't an object—it's the original oath, held in the memory of the first warden's ghost, who demands Ulyana prove herself worthy. Emotional beat: judgment; she must testify to who she truly is.

chapters.title: The Longest Night Begins
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The gilded court, desperate, tears the veil fully open; true winter falls across both realms at once. Emotional beat: apocalypse; the clock runs out.

chapters.title: March to the Spire
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The found family fights through the frozen vanguard to the covenant spire at Thornfell's heart. Emotional beat: resolve; ordinary outcasts marching on eternity.

chapters.title: Serapha Stands
chapters.summary: Serapha's POV. The order arrives—not to stop Ulyana but to hold the line behind her, Serapha publicly confessing the forgery. Emotional beat: restitution; justice finally spoken aloud, though too late for law.

chapters.title: The Sacrifice Clause
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the spire, the oath demands a warden bound forever to the mountain—no leaving, no ordinary life. Ulyana realizes the prophecy never promised survival of her old self. Emotional beat: reckoning; counting what belonging costs.

chapters.title: Theo's Choice
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo offers himself as warden instead, claiming author's descent entitles him. Ulyana refuses; the mountain accepts only her. Emotional beat: love tested; he tries to carry what isn't his.

chapters.title: Reforge the Covenant
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Climax. Ulyana unites the keystones, speaks the old oath in both tongues, and lets the mountain claim her—storms answering not as weapons but as voice. Emotional beat: transcendence; exile ends by becoming the thing between realms.

chapters.title: Winter Breaks
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The long winter shatters; the hollow court is rekindled under Vess's heir; the gilded court is stripped of power. Emotional beat: dawn; the world exhales.

chapters.title: Warden of Thornfell
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana adjusts to her new existence—bound to the peaks but able to walk where storms go, which is everywhere. Emotional beat: bittersweet freedom; she traded one cage for a wider sky.

chapters.title: The Family That Stayed
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The outcasts build a village at the mountain's foot; Theo stays, writing a new book—not prophecy, just record. Emotional beat: homecoming; belonging chosen, not granted.

chapters.title: Storm-Caller's Blessing
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Epilogue. On the first anniversary, Ulyana sends a gentle rain over Marrowgate's rebuilt fields and feels her family below look up. Emotional beat: peace; justice outside the law, belonging beyond borders.
